newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major calls Labour inflation pledge absurd.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major calls Labour inflation pledge absurd.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major on Wednesday dismissed as absurd the main opposition Labour party's contention that it will be just as tough on inflation as the Conservative government.

"It's silly, isn't it? I mean, the concept of a Labour party, based on all their history, all their instincts, the nature of their parliamentary party actually being more successful on inflation than the present government, is just absurd isn't it?" Major told reporters.

He was commenting on a pledge by Labour's economic spokesman, Gordon Brown, to at least match the government's inflation target of 2.5 percent or less. Brown is due to disclose his exact target in a speech later on Wednesday.
Major said Labour had opposed all the steps his government had taken to bring down inflation in the past five years.

"Suddenly we are expected to believe they have changed totally and would keep inflation down. I don't believe it for a second and I don't believe the British public will either," the prime minister said.
